edits.value_json: 四 means “four.” In its present form, it has an enclosing 囗 shape around inner 儿-form strokes. This visible structure does not settle its disputed origin: proposals include four counting rods, or a graph for 呬 (breath) or 泗 (nasal discharge) later reused for “four.”

The current graph is structurally an enclosing 囗 with inner 儿-form strokes; this modern description does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those shapes. Ancient analyses remain disputed. One interprets four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four. Another proposes that 四 was a graph for 呬 depicting breath, later reused for “four” because of sound similarity. A separate proposal treats it as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for “four”; its proponent noted that the proposal lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing account is established, and the depicted referent’s original name is unknown.
